metadata.notes: Dry heat: unlike FRY/BOIL, no medium ingredient is required at all — requiredIngredientCapabilities is deliberately empty, not just satisfied by something ambient.
metadata.retrySafeNote: retrySafe: true (data-level, no duplication) — but re-baking an already-done target risks drying it out/overcooking, same culinary caveat as fry.json/boil.json's cooking actions.
metadata.actionKindNote: Song, Huang, Sun, Tian, Wang & Li, arXiv:2608.04768 (2026, PAPER_NOTES_2608.04768.md, REFERENCES.md): the paper's own 'heating' example, in an oven rather than a liquid/oil medium — a real, elapsed-time thermal process. No place.ts/oven wiring exists at all yet (oven.json has no thermophysical data) — applyAction executes it atomically today, an honest gap this field makes explicit rather than hides.
metadata.maxDurationSecondsNote: HOUSE VALUE, not independently sourced (this action has no durationSeconds parameter to reuse a max from at all — its own gap, unrelated to this ticket). 5400s (90 minutes) is a generous outer bound covering typical home-oven baking tasks (most baked dishes finish well under 90 minutes); hitting it indicates something has gone wrong (wrong temperature, wrong dish), not a legitimately slow bake. Not derived from any specific cited dish or source.
metadata.requiresActiveAttentionNote: Added 2026-08-17 (DAG-execution ticket, action.ts's own requiresActiveAttention doc comment) — classified PASSIVE. Oven-driven dry heat, the archetypal 'walk away and come back' technique — nothing for an actor to do once the dish is in the oven.

verification.description: Internal temperature has risen to the expected range for the target's baked state (weakest verification in this vocabulary — oven air temperature is not the target's actual internal temperature, and no probe is assumed present)

hazards.note: Oven cavity and bakeware — sustained high-temperature contact burn risk, worse than a stovetop pan (larger hot surface, less visibility of what's inside)
